A follow-up question on the max.time argument.
I'm looking for the default setting of max.time. Does anyone know where I can find this?

Thanks!

Sanne

> Menglin,

> jagcontrol=list(max.time="5m")

messages.body_plain:
Sanne,

For automatic convergence, blavaan uses the autorun.jags() function from the runjags package. The default is Inf, i.e., run forever if you need to. Further detail is in the autorun.jags help file:

?runjags::autorun.jags

Best,
Ed

messages.subject: Re: How to set the maximum number of iteration in blavaan?
messages.subject_clean: How to set the maximum number of iteration in blavaan?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ed, thanks for your reply!!

I think I would prefer to have the same default setting as in jags (max.time=inf). Any other setting in blavaan would also be fine, but in that case it would be helpful to mention this in the blavaan documentation, to make users aware of this default setting (I was running a simulation study, in which convergence was set to 'auto' based on a stricter PSRF criterion (< 1.01), but I still was left with some data sets that were not converged and had a higher PSRF criterion than the one I specified, because of the max.time setting I was unaware of.).

Best,

Sanne

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed

Was looking at an interesting problem. If we have participants with different lags between measurements, we would like to include different fix values for the latent slope in the growth curve model.

I know this cannot be done directly in lavaan or blavaan. I can edit the JAGS code to include person specific factor loadings. Is there a way to add the different factor loadings with the mcmcextra argument?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: person specific loadings for growth curves
messages.subject_clean: person specific loadings for growth curves
messages.body_plain:
I think I need to add a "data" argument to mcmcextra for this. Then you could specify a highly informative prior around the extra time information (which is like fixing to a constant). blavaan can only fix a parameter to a single value or assign a prior to it, so the prior is the best bet.

If/when I add a data argument, it would be possible to do something like

i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3
s =~ 1*x1 + prior("dnorm(time2[i], 1e4)")*x2 + prior("dnorm(time3[i], 1e4)")*x3

Then send "time2" and "time3" variables in via mcmcextra. It will go on the TODO list.

Ed
